name: Inflame Appliances Ltd
title: Inflame Appliances Ltd - 541083 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 chimney demand fell sharply (Q4 revenue about INR35-37 crore vs INR55-60 crore expected) with raw material share rising 70% to 75%; management guides 50% FY27 growth and 4 lakh chimneys, but no numeric margin guidance and heavy China dependence persists.

triggers.label: Q4 revenue INR35-37 crore vs INR55-60 expected
triggers.quote: We were expecting the last quarter to be like INR55 crores, INR60 crores, but it was like INR35 crores, INR36 crores, INR37 crores maybe.

triggers.label: Inventory high: 40-50% carried for imports
triggers.quote: the 40%, 50% inventory that we are carrying will be over, sir.

triggers.label: FY27 target 4 lakh chimneys, 50% growth
triggers.quote: We are targeting 4 lakh chimneys this year.

triggers.label: Demand recovered in Apr-May, 2 months of growth
triggers.quote: Sir, demand has recovered. The demand has recovered.

summary.headline: Inflame guides FY27 chimney volumes to ~4 lakh (+45-50%) and Q4 FY26 demand was soft, with management reporting June-to-date recovery.
summary.overview: Management said FY26 revenue grew about 41-42% and EBITDA about 55%, with EPS up about 85%, but Q4 was weak as market demand softened and raw material costs rose to about 75% of revenue in H2 from about 70% in H1. Q4 revenue was about INR35-37 crore against an internal expectation of INR55-60 crore. Management said demand has recovered in the first two months of FY27, with monthly growth of 40-50%, and that it is tracking its 50% growth target. Price pass-through is not complete and is expected to finish in about 1.5-2 months, with efficiency and AI-based inspection offsets. The company also disclosed a 34% stake in a new BLDC motor and electronics associate, Tricoree Machmatrix, though no investment figures were given.

financial_highlights.change: vs 195,000 units in prior year (about 38% growth)

financial_highlights.value: about 75% of revenue in H2 vs about 70% in H1
financial_highlights.change: up about 4-5 percentage points; main increase in Q4
vs internal expectation of INR55-60 crore
revenue growth about 11%, per analyst question; not disputed by management

segments.name: Chimneys
segments.commentary: Core product; Panchkula grew about 42% and Hyderabad about 31% in volume. Management expects chimneys to remain about 60-65% of revenue going forward.

segments.name: Built-in / new products (ovens, wine coolers, refrigerators, microwaves, dishwashers, hobs)
segments.commentary: Other products were about 5-10% of revenue in the past one to two years. Management said 25 new models were showcased in April; built-in ovens are being ramped, with dishwashers and microwaves targeted by December-January. Hobs BIS is expected to be finalised in September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: about 4 lakh chimneys (about 50% growth on 270,000) and about 45-50% growth in chimney volume and total revenue.
Revenue target of INR400 crore-plus in FY28, and INR500 crore in FY28-FY29, per management.
Gross margin expected to recover as price pass-through completes in about 1.5-2 months; management said it will absorb pressure through efficiency gains and expects some margin pressure in H1 FY27.
BLDC share of chimney production expected to rise to about 80% by end of FY27 from about 60% currently.
Management expects inventory of 40-50% to fall once motors and PCBs are made in India, timeline about 1-2 years.
capex_capacity: Panchkula CapEx of about INR10 crore for 50,000 sq ft of new construction; ground floor operational within days, adding about 12,000-15,000 chimneys of capacity; second part by 15 August and third by 30 September.
Hyderabad plant utilisation is not being prioritised; it is being used for premium and value-added products (built-in ovens, wine coolers, refrigerators, microwaves, dishwashers).
Tricoree Machmatrix Private Limited: associate with 34% Inflame stake, to manufacture BLDC motors first (about 1-1.5 years) then electronics (another 1-1.5 years); no investment amount disclosed.
Flamecraft (Hyderabad): Inflame holds 51% of sheet metal business; company is outsourcing sheet metal and other processes via joint ventures.
Management plans glass plant with zero manpower, to be considered once investment crosses INR250-300 crore; not yet committed.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 demand was soft; management attributed it to the Gulf/geopolitical situation and said major buyers (IFB, Crompton, Hindware, Havells) were short of orders.
Management said demand has recovered in April-May 2026, with monthly volumes above prior-year levels for two months; price negotiations are ongoing with some customers.
Price pass-through not 100%; management cited rupee depreciation, Middle East disruption, RMB appreciation and gas supply issues (about three weeks) as cost drivers.
Management claims complaint rate below 1.5% versus higher rates for Chinese suppliers; cites 10-year warranty products.
Approval cycle for new products: about 15 days to 1 month for KAFF; about 2-2.5 months for Hindware, Havells, IFB, Crompton.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 FY26 below the expected 30,000-32,000 chimneys per month?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to industry demand softness and geopolitical fears; major buyers were short of orders in Q4. No loss of orders was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Are you on track for 4 lakh chimneys in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said 270,000 in FY26 plus 50% growth implies about 4 lakh, and said the order position covers the planned growth for 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue growth only about 11% on about 20% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material share rose to about 75%, plus INR depreciation and gas supply issues; volume weakness was from market demand.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold on 50% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins may be slightly lower but absolute profit should rise; AI-based inspection is expected to cut inspection time by 10-20% in 1-1.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company still on SME rather than main board?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not meet two criteria: paid-up capital of at least INR10 crore and net worth of at least INR75 crore. Will migrate once eligible.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high and what about exports?
qa_highlights.answer: High inventory reflects SKD/CKD imports for refrigerators, ovens and hobs; expected to fall with local manufacturing. Exports are being explored, but India OEM demand of about 6 lakh chimneys is the priority.

risks_watch: Dependence on China for BLDC motors, PCBs, switches and heating elements; BLDC motors reportedly 37-38% sourced from China, and possible BIS on motors.
Raw material and currency pressure: RMB appreciation, rupee depreciation and Middle East disruption; full price pass-through not yet achieved.
Q4 FY26 demand weakness; management says recovery is under way but sustainability depends on market sentiment.
Execution risk on new products (built-in ovens, dishwashers, microwaves) and hobs BIS timing (expected September).
Inventory levels remain high (about 40-50%) until local manufacturing starts.
Promoter stake-raise considered only after Diwali; main board migration depends on net worth and paid-up capital thresholds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order book, with an upbeat outlook for FY27; evasive on the Tricoree JV investment amount, the Q4 shortfall figures, and the stock price and main board questions. Management also deferred several questions on the Hyderabad plant and exports.
